why did we lose x in '= Θ( n + n · ∫₁ⁿ x / x² dx )
= Θ( n + n · ∫₁ⁿ 1/x dx )"
`x / x² = x / (x·x) = 1/x`. One factor of `x` cancels.
messages.reasoning:
The user is asking about a step in the Akra-Bazzi method derivation. They're looking at this sequence:

T(n) = Θ( n^1 + n^1 · ∫₁ⁿ x / x^{1+1} dx )
= Θ( n + n · ∫₁ⁿ x / x² dx )
= Θ( n + n · ∫₁ⁿ 1/x dx )

They're asking why `x / x²` simplifies to `1/x`.

This is basic algebra: x / x² = 1/x (since x/x² = 1/x^{2-1} = 1/x¹ = 1/x). The x in the numerator cancels with one factor of x in the denominator.
